Owner views on equipment financing in fitness studios

Abstract
We report a questionnaire answered by 318 studio owners in four countries. Respondents rated financing options on a five-point Likert scale.

1. Introduction
Paragraph 1 on equipment-dependent services describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

2. Methods
The survey instrument had 24 items. Respondents were owners or managers. We invited 1,050 studios and 318 replied (response rate 30.3%). Paragraph 1 on the questionnaire describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

Paragraph 2 on the questionnaire describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

3. Results
Most respondents preferred leasing over bank loans (62%). Based on the November 2026 web snapshot, standalone studios hold a market share of 40%.

4. Discussion
Paragraph 1 on owner preferences describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

Paragraph 2 on owner preferences describes the setting in plain terms. Prior studies report mixed evidence on this question (Smith, 2019; Jones and Lee, 2021). We keep the units of observation distinct and report each step with its sample size.

5. Limitations
Respondents chose to answer, so non-response bias is possible.

6. Conclusion
Owners prefer leasing; the survey does not measure market share.

References
